claim_verdicts.evidence: Re-extracted this round: `git -C examples/don-hang show stage-1:DonHang.Infrastructure/LoggingNotifier.cs` lines 9-13 match the lesson's block character-for-character, including `public void Send(int orderId, string subject) => logger.LogInformation("notification for order {OrderId}: {Subject}", orderId, subject);`. One message template, two named placeholders, two arguments after the template.

Re-extracted this round: `git -C examples/don-hang show stage-1:DonHang.Api/Middleware/RequestLoggingMiddleware.cs` lines 9-24 match the lesson's block character-for-character, including the template "{Method} {Path} responded {StatusCode} in {ElapsedMs}ms" followed by context.Request.Method, context.Request.Path, context.Response.StatusCode, stopwatch.ElapsedMilliseconds. Four placeholders, four arguments, same order.

"Each log API uses a message template. The message template can contain placeholders for which arguments are provided. Use names for the placeholders, not numbers. The order of placeholders, not their names, determines which parameters are used to provide their values." and "The arguments themselves are passed to the logging system, not just the formatted message template. This enables logging providers to store the parameter values as fields." The note "The names aren't used to align the arguments to the placeholders" settles "matched by position, not by name".

Re-run live 2026-09-25 against the running lab: login, then POST /api/v1/orders returned 201; `docker logs donhang-api --since 30s` printed "info: DonHang.Infrastructure.LoggingNotifier[0]" then the indented "notification for order 28: order placed", plus exactly two RequestLoggingMiddleware lines (login 200, order 201) - Try it's expected result holds as written. Container runs ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development with no console-formatter override and no appsettings.Development.json at stage-1, so this is the default simple console formatter.
claim_verdicts.source: live: docker logs donhang-api --since 30s; examples/don-hang @ stage-1 docker-compose.yml (api), DonHang.Api/appsettings.json

claim_verdicts.evidence: "If an interpolated string has the type `string`, the compiler typically transforms it into a String.Format method call. The compiler can replace String.Format with String.Concat if the analyzed behavior would be equivalent to concatenation." and "The compiler checks if an interpolated string is assigned to a type that satisfies the interpolated string handler pattern." LoggerExtensions.LogInformation takes `string? message`, not a handler type, so the value is finished before the call - the condition the claim carries.

`git show stage-1:DonHang.Domain/OrderService.cs`: PlaceOrderAsync ends `await repository.AddAsync(order); await repository.SaveChangesAsync(); notifier.Send(order.Id, "order placed"); return order;` (line 21), with no condition around the Send. Confirmed live this round: one POST /api/v1/orders produced exactly one "notification for order 28: order placed" line. The other call site, notifier.Send(order.Id, "order cancelled") in CancelOrderAsync, is not what the lesson cites.

Each class holds exactly one LogInformation call at stage-1: LoggingNotifier's templates {OrderId} and {Subject}; RequestLoggingMiddleware's templates {Method}, {Path}, {StatusCode}, {ElapsedMs}. The two placeholder sets are disjoint - no StatusCode on the notification event, no OrderId on the request event. Checked by re-reading both files at the tag this round.

First half verified live: POST /api/v1/orders with {"items":[]} returned 400 and PATCH /api/v1/orders/999999/cancel returned 404, each producing only an ExceptionHandlingMiddleware warning and NO RequestLoggingMiddleware line. Second half is too broad: not every validation/not-found error in this app throws. `GET /api/v1/orders/999999` (OrdersController.Get returns NotFound()) logged "GET /api/v1/orders/999999 responded 404 in 27ms", and {"items":"oops"} - a validation error from [ApiController] model binding - logged "POST /api/v1/orders responded 400 in 1ms".
claim_verdicts.source: live 2026-09-25: docker exec donhang-lab curl ... ; docker logs donhang-api --since 6s; OrdersController.cs, ExceptionHandlingMiddleware.cs @ stage-1
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: RequestLoggingMiddleware's LogInformation runs only after `await next(context)` returns, so a request whose handler throws (PlaceOrderAsync's ArgumentException, CancelOrderAsync's KeyNotFoundException) skips it and its 4xx never appears as StatusCode. A 4xx the app returns without throwing - Get's NotFound(), or [ApiController]'s model-validation 400 - is logged normally.

issues.text: `Stopwatch` is not ASP.NET Core. It comes from `System.Diagnostics` - the file's first line is `using System.Diagnostics;` - a .NET base-library type any console app can use; the project references no package for it. `RequestDelegate` and `HttpContext` are the ASP.NET Core part (Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http), and `ILogger<T>` in the constructor is neither, which the sentence also sweeps into "ASP.NET Core plumbing".
issues.fix: Write: "The constructor parameters, `HttpContext`, `next(context)`, and the `Stopwatch` timing are plumbing from ASP.NET Core and the .NET base library, not this lesson's focus - only the template string and its four arguments matter here."

issues.text: "on every log event" over-generalises what the preceding sentences established. Named fields exist only on events whose call passed a template with named placeholders. This app logs events with none: ExceptionHandlingMiddleware's `logger.LogWarning(ex, "request rejected as invalid")` has no placeholders, so its event carries no named field at all. As written, a reader can take it to mean every line in `docker logs donhang-api` carries fields.
issues.fix: Scope it to the calls under discussion: "This app doesn't run such a tool yet - the fields exist regardless, on every event these template calls produce, whether or not anything reads them that way today."
issues.quote: the fields exist regardless, on every log event, whether or not anything reads them that way today
